articles.title: Australia CPI Rises to 4.3% as Underlying Inflation Exceeds Forecasts
articles.expand: Australia’s annual CPI inflation accelerated from 4.0% to 4.3% in September, exceeding market expectations of 4.2%, while monthly prices rose 0.8%. For Q3, headline CPI increased 1.3% q/q and 3.9% y/y, both matching forecasts. With a hike close to fully priced, the hold is likely to hit the New Zealand dollar and pull front-end yields lower. The 4-3 split and the guidance that tighter policy is still likely should limit how far December pricing unwinds. Policy divergence is now sharp. articles.expand: MUFG’s call puts the risk squarely on the New Zealand dollar: with a hike almost fully priced, the currency’s G10 outperformance this month depends on the RBNZ endorsing a much steeper path than MUFG expects. articles.expand: The services PPI is rarely a big mover for the yen on its own, but a reading at or above 3.7% would reinforce December hike pricing and lend modest support to the yen and short-dated JGB yields into Friday. A downside surprise would carry more weight than usual, coming after the sharp September slowdown in goods producer prices, and could lean against the yen by encouraging talk of a slower BoJ path.
